column3: 'Showpad holds what no other system has: the content, coaching signals, and deal-stage context that defines how your company wins. Connect your stack, and that foundation flows everywhere it needs to go.' (https://www.showpad.com/)

column7: INTERPRETATION (analyst view, not capability claims): The shared-memory whitespace narrows further in this batch. Showpad's homepage states it 'holds what no other system has: the content, coaching signals, and deal-stage context' — the closest direct claim to PitchSense's one-shared-memory frame among the ten homepages inspected across batches 1-3. Salesloft's 'Signals' concept and Mindtickle's 'decade of rep behavior data... compounding' are adjacent but framed as signal-capture and behavior-data assets rather than a single connected memory. Testing question: can PitchSense's 'one memory connecting four intelligences' be differentiated from Showpad's foundation claim by depth of connection (calls+CRM+emails+Slack+documents in one memory) rather than by existence of a foundation? Showpad's claim is a vendor statement, not verified architecture.

column4: 'AI Sales Role Play' + 'Scale coaching with AI-powered role-plays so your reps can master their pitches before money is on the line' + hero CTA 'Try AI Role Play' (https://www.mindtickle.com/ + https://www.mindtickle.com/solutions/sales-leadership-solutions-training/)

column7: INTERPRETATION: Coaching and roleplay are prominently claimed by three of the four inspected vendors — a material change from batches 1-2 where AI roleplay was unfeatured on homepages. Mindtickle promotes 'Try AI Role Play' as a hero CTA (to a dedicated roleplay product site, roleplay.mindtickle.com) and cites Cisco's roleplay results (31% deal size); Allego has AI Role Play & Coaching as a top-level nav product; Showpad features Roleplay AI as a Genie product. Salesloft's inspected pages showed no roleplay proposition (page-scoped observation). PitchSense's 'AI roleplay as additional differentiation' hypothesis is weakened against the three inspected enablement vendors that prominently promote it (Mindtickle, Allego, Showpad — not Salesloft) — roleplay is prominently featured messaging among these inspected vendors (Phase 1 roleplay specialists should be checked before generalizing beyond these vendors). Testing question: what remains distinctive about PitchSense's roleplay (memory-grounded scenarios from real deals?) vs. these established offerings?
